Thanks — useful brief. I’ll design a 12‑week, upper‑body focused progression that respects the physio restriction: only pain‑free range of motion, no overhead loading on the right (affected) side. Because she’s a recreational climber and an office worker, the plan emphasizes shoulder rehabilitation (scapular control, rotator cuff, posterior capsule mobility), balanced strength for climbing, posture correction (thoracic mobility, scapular retractors), and gradual return to heavier horizontal and pulling work while avoiding painful or unsupported overhead pressing on the right. I’ll give phases, weekly structure, session-by-session details (exercises, sets, reps), and brief nutrition/recovery notes.

Important safety notes to pass to client:
- Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain, reproduction of her impingement pain, or progressive pain after sessions — only work in pain‑free range per physio.
- Use conservative progression: increase load only when she can complete all sets/reps with good form and no pain.
- Reassess with physio if symptoms change. 
- Warm up thoroughly before each session (general cardio 5–8 min + shoulder-specific dynamic warm-up).

Overview — structure and emphasis
- Frequency: 3 gym sessions per week (Upper-focused). Optional 1–2 low-impact cardio or climbing technique sessions in pain‑free range during later phases. Include 2 rest/active recovery days.
- Workout length: 50–70 minutes.
- Progression across 3 phases (4 weeks each):
  Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Rehabilitation & motor control — low load, high quality, emphasis on scapular stability, rotator cuff endurance, thoracic mobility, posterior chain activation, and isometric/no‑overhead patterns for the right shoulder.
  Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength & hypertrophy for upper back and pulling, introduce controlled loaded horizontal pressing and unilateral work avoiding overhead on right; progressive load increase.
  Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength transfer and climbing-specific strength endurance; heavier rows/pull patterns, increased unilateral work, introduce supported/modified overhead loading if cleared and pain‑free (I’ll give alternatives otherwise).

Session template (3 sessions/week): Two primary upper sessions + one accessory/mixed session.
- Session A: Horizontal push/pull emphasis + rotator cuff/scapular control.
- Session B: Vertical pull + posterior chain and thoracic mobility + rotator cuff.
- Session C: Accessory + unilateral strength + scapular endurance + climbing-specific conditioning (finger/crimp training only if cleared and pain‑free).

Warm-up (every session, 8–12 min)
1. General 5 min light cardio (bike/row/elliptical).
2. Shoulder-specific dynamic warm-up (perform slowly, pain‑free):
   - Wall slides (or scapular slide) 2 × 10
   - Y‑T‑W progressions lying on incline bench or Swiss ball 2 × 8 each
   - Banded pull‑apart (scapular retraction emphasis) 2 × 15 light
   - Thoracic rotation with half‑kneeling or lying on side 1–2 × 8 each side
   - Low‑load rotator cuff warmers: side‑lying external rotation (pain‑free) 2 × 12 light / or standing with light band 2 × 15

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Rehab & control
Goal: Build scapular control, rotator cuff endurance and posture. Low loads, higher reps, emphasis on pain‑free motor control.

Week 1–2 (three sessions/week)
Session A
- Warm-up
- Isometric scapular set (prone Y hold on bench at ~30°): 3 × 10 s
- Incline/bench-supported chest press (neutral grip) — two‑arm if pain‑free: 3 × 10–12 (light)
  *If any right discomfort, swap for single‑arm supported horizontal press with left doing light load and right performing isometric hold.*
- Seated cable row (chest‑supported if available) — slow eccentric: 3 × 12
- Banded face pulls (high to mid, focus scapular retraction/ER): 3 × 15
- Side‑lying external rotation (right and left) — pain‑free: 3 × 12 each
- Prone scapular retractions on incline bench (squeeze lower traps): 3 × 12
- Biceps curl (light) or banded biceps: 2 × 12
- Pec stretch & posterior capsule sleeper stretch (gentle, only pain‑free) 2 × 30 s

Session B
- Warm-up
- TRX or ring rows (adjust angle to maintain pain‑free motion): 4 × 8–10
- Single‑arm supported lat pulldown (left full ROM, right pain‑free partial ROM/no overhead load): 3 × 10
- Dumbbell prone Y/T/W on incline bench: 3 × 8 each
- Banded external rotation at 0° for rotator cuff endurance: 3 × 15
- Scapular clock (standing, move scapula in 8 directions) 3 rounds
- Hip hinge/hip‑dominant posterior chain: Romanian deadlift with light kettlebell/dumbbell: 3 × 10
- Cervical/thoracic mobilization & foam rolling 5 min

Session C
- Warm-up
- Isometric ER at 45° abduction against wall (pain‑free): 4 × 10 s
- Single‑arm supported chest press on incline (left heavier, right isometric or light): 3 × 10
- Cable horizontal abduction (reverse fly) at chest height: 3 × 12
- Scapular rhythmic stabilization on wall (push into wall, small pulses): 3 × 20 s
- Farmer carry with neutral shoulder (light/moderate) 3 × 30–40 m
- Grip/finger endurance (climbing board or holds only if cleared): 3 × 15–30 s openhand holds
- Mobility: thoracic foam roll + doorway pec stretch 2 × 30 s

Week 3–4 (three sessions/week)
Progression: Increase loading slightly or add 1–2 reps per set if pain‑free. Increase rotator cuff volume.

Session A
- Warm-up
- Incline dumbbell press (support under chest if needed) — neutral/pronated as tolerated: 3 × 8–10
- Chest‑supported row (dumbbell or machine): 4 × 8–10
- Banded face pull with external rotation finish: 3 × 15
- Side‑lying ER + standing banded ER superset: 3 × 12 each
- Prone scapular retractions: 3 × 15
- Dead bug/core control: 3 × 10 each

Session B
- Warm-up
- Supported single‑arm lat pulldown or neutral‑grip pulldown (left heavier, right controlled): 4 × 8–10
- TRX row progressed angle: 4 × 8–10
- Prone Y/T/W combo sets: 3 rounds
- Banded low‑row hold (isometric at full scapular squeeze): 3 × 12 s
- Romanian deadlift moderate: 3 × 8–10
- Thoracic rotation with banded distraction: 2 × 10 each

Session C
- Warm-up
- Horizontal pressing (machine or cable): 3 × 10
- Cable or single‑arm biceps + triceps light supersets: 3 × 12
- External rotation dropset (band): work to fatigue but pain‑free
- Scapular push‑ups (knees if needed): 3 × 12–15
- Farmer carry/loaded walk (progress distance/weight): 3 × 40–60 m
- Mobility/calm down incl. gentle rotator cuff flossing

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Strength & balanced hypertrophy
Goal: Increase strength in horizontal press/pull and scapular stabilizers, introduce unilateral pushing and heavier pulling while still avoiding unsupported overhead loading on right. Start loading left more unilaterally to build symmetry and safe compensation.

General progression notes:
- Use moderate loads (RPE 6–8).
- Continue high rotator cuff volume (2–3x/week).
- Tempo control, slow eccentrics.

Week 5–6
Session A
- Warm-up
- Supported single‑arm chest press (dumbbell on bench with trunk support) — left heavier, right low load/isometric as needed: 4 × 6–8
- Bent‑over chest‑supported dumbbell row: 4 × 8
- Seated cable row (heavyish) 3 × 6–8 (slow eccentric)
- Banded face pull 3 × 15
- Side‑lying ER + prone horizontal abduction (reverse fly) superset: 3 × 10 each
- Core plank variations 3 × 30–45 s

Session B
- Warm-up
- Neutral‑grip pull‑ups or assisted pull‑ups (use band/assisted machine): 4 × 4–6 (if too painful, do heavy negative reps or lat pulldown)
- One‑arm dumbbell row (left heavier; right supported on bench and light): 4 × 6–8 each side
- Landmine or cable horizontal press (keeps shoulder lower than overhead): 3 × 8–10
- Banded external rotation 3 × 15
- Single‑leg Romanian deadlift 3 × 8 each
- Thoracic extension work 3 × 8–10

Session C
- Warm-up
- Incline cable press (neutral grip) or machine press 3 × 8
- Chest‑supported high row 3 × 10 (focus mid traps)
- Scapular pull‑ups / scapular depressions 3 × 10
- Farmer carry or suitcase carry (unilateral load left/heavier) 3 × 40–60 m
- Grip/climbing holds (short duration, open‑hand) 4 × 20–30 s
- Rotator cuff circuit: band ER, band IR, prone T 2 rounds × 12 each

Week 7–8
Increase load/reduce reps for strength sets and add a heavier session.

Session A
- Warm-up
- Flat chest-supported dumbbell press or single-arm cable press: 4 × 5–6 (left heavier; right limited)
- Heavy chest‑supported row or T‑bar row (neutral grip): 4 × 6–8
- Banded face pull 4 × 12
- Side‑lying ER + cable IR (light) 3 × 12 each
- Deadlift variation (trap bar/light conventional) 3 × 5–6

Session B
- Warm-up
- Weighted pull-ups / heavy assisted / eccentric emphasis: 5 × 3–5
- One‑arm dumbbell row heavy (left) / right supported 4 × 6
- Landmine single‑arm press (left) — right avoid or perform isometric hold: 3 × 6 each
- Scapular stabilizer circuit (prone Y/T/W + wall slides) 3 rounds
- Farmer carry heavy 3 × 30–40 m

Session C
- Warm-up
- Cable cross horizontal press 3 × 8–10
- Seated cable row narrow + wide grip superset 3 × 8–10
- Rotator cuff 3 × 15 (band ER/IR)
- Climbing‑specific: repeaters on campus board only if cleared (short, pain‑free), or long open‑hand hangs lighter: 4 × 10–15 s on / 50 s off
- Mobility and thoracic extension 10 min

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Strength transfer, power/endurance for climbing
Goal: Increase pulling strength, unilateral stability, and endurance. If the physio clears and there’s no pain, introduce supported/modified overhead loading for right (e.g., landmine press, single‑arm push press with light load and support). If not cleared, maintain no unsupported overhead — use landmine/leaned/neutral patterns.

Week 9–10
Session A
- Warm-up
- Flat single‑arm dumbbell press (left heavier; right light & controlled or isometric): 4 × 5–6
- Chest‑supported heavy row: 4 × 6
- Incline cable press neutral grip: 3 × 8
- Banded face pull + external rotation superset: 3 × 12
- Heavy farmer carry 3 × 30–40 m

Session B
- Warm-up
- Weighted pull‑ups or heavy eccentric pull‑ups: 5 × 3–5
- Single‑arm landmine row or heavy one‑arm cable row: 4 × 6–8
- Supported overhead pattern (landmine press/leaning single‑arm press) — left heavier, right only if pain‑free and supported: 3 × 6
- Rotator cuff circuit 3 rounds
- Core anti‑rotation (Pallof press) 3 × 10 each

Session C
- Warm-up
- Cluster/contrast for pulling endurance: 6 sets of 3 chin-ups (submaximal) with 90 s rest, then 2 min rest, repeat 3 rounds
- Horizontal pressing accessory 3 × 8
- Grip & finger endurance: repeaters or longer open‑hand hangs 6 × 10–12 s or 4 × 20–30 s depending on tolerance
- Mobility: posterior capsule, pec stretch, thoracic extension

Week 11–12
Peaking strength-endurance and preparation to return more fully to climbing.

Session A
- Warm-up
- Single‑arm dumbbell press heavy for left / right limited: 4 × 4–6
- Heavy chest‑supported row 4 × 5
- Banded face pull 4 × 12
- Rotator cuff finishers 3 × 15
- Carry/loaded carries 3 × 30–60 m

Session B
- Warm-up
- Weighted/assisted pull‑ups: 5 × 3–5 (aim to increase load)
- One‑arm rows heavy 4 × 6
- If pain‑free and cleared, controlled single‑arm push press with light load (right only if pain‑free and physiotherapist agrees), otherwise landmine press: 3 × 5
- Climbing-specific endurance circuit (submaximal pulling, 2–3 sets): e.g., 5–6 routes or laps at 60–70% effort or antigravity repeaters on campus/board within tolerance
- Mobility & recovery

Session C
- Warm-up
- Mixed accessory: cable cross, triceps, biceps 3 × 8–12
- Scapular endurance: scapular pull‑ups, scapular push‑ups 3 × 12–15
- Rotator cuff heavy volume 3 × 20 (band)
- Longer grip session (if tolerated) 4 × 30–40 s open‑hand hangs
- Deload mobility and plan review with physio

Additional program notes and exercise substitution options
- Avoid unsupported overhead pressing on the right. Substitutes include landmine press, incline presses, and two‑arm supported presses. Left side can be loaded more unilaterally to maintain strength symmetry.
- For any pressing movement, prefer neutral grips when possible to take strain off the anterior shoulder.
- Chest‑supported rows and chest‑supported presses reduce scapular instability and are safe early options.
- Rotator cuff work: prioritize external rotation and scapular retraction drills — 2–3×/week.
- If client progresses without pain, consider gradual reinstatement of overhead work under physio guidance in Phase 3 only.

Load and progression guidance
- Start conservative: choose load that allows full sets with 2 reps in reserve (RPE ~7) and no pain.
- Increase load 2–5% when all prescribed sets/reps are completed with good form and no soreness increase.
- For rehab/rotator cuff sets use slow tempo (3–4 s eccentrics), control, and higher reps.

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Protein: aim for ~1.2–1.6 g/kg bodyweight per day to support muscle repair and climbing adaptations. If weight/goal specifics provided I can refine.
- Calories: maintain slight calorie surplus if hypertrophy/strength gains desired, otherwise maintenance for performance.
- Hydration and sleep: prioritize 7–9 hours sleep/night. Aim for consistent sleep schedule to support recovery.
- Anti‑inflammatory management: use ice/heat only per physio guidance. Avoid relying on NSAIDs long‑term without medical advice.
- Post‑session: 10–15 min cool down with thoracic mobilization and gentle rotator cuff activation; avoid prolonged immobilization of shoulder.

Climbing return-to-play suggestions
- Keep climbing technical, short, easy routes initially (≤50% of max), focusing on footwork and body position.
- Avoid sustained overhead reach on the right; translate training gains into closed‑chain pulling (horizontal and vertical) first.
- Gradually increase climbing intensity in Phase 3 if asymptomatic.

Monitoring and reassessment
- Track pain (0–10) during/after sessions. Any increase >2 from baseline or sharp pains warrants stop and physio consult.
- Reassess ROM, scapular control, and max pull/press every 4 weeks; adjust program based on progress and physio feedback.

If you want, I can:
- Turn this into a printable week‑by‑week spreadsheet with daily checkboxes and progression loads.
- Customize loads and specific starting weights if you provide current lifts/1RMs or perceived RPEs for key movements.
- Add a climbing‑specific microcycle for an upcoming climbing event.

Would you like the plan exported as a printable 12‑week calendar or do you want me to set starting loads for her based on estimated abilities?
